title: PackagingTargets
description: Release build-input matrix (build side, P5-01). One entry per release target of xresconv-gui; a target may ship several artifacts (see @xresconv/packaging matrix). Scope frozen by decisions D1 (64-bit only, docs/plan/records/P0-06.md) and the 2026-09-28 portable-archive decision: Windows ships a zip (no installer; WebView2 Evergreen plus an in-archive bootstrapper sidecar), Linux ships distro-independent tar.zst archives (offline also as AppImage; no deb/rpm), macOS keeps the dmg installer. This file holds build-time identity/policy only; fields that can only be filled at build time (appVersion, sourceCommit, hashes, files, signingEvidence, buildToolchain, repositorySnapshot, verificationReport) live in the artifact-side runtime-manifest.json (schema packaging-runtime-manifest). Semantic rules (duplicates, baseline set equality, per-os strategy coherence) are enforced by @xresconv/packaging on top of this structural schema.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema file.

schemaVersion.description: Format version of this targets file. Breaking changes must bump it.

targets.description: Explicit enumeration of every release target; CI aggregate jobs compare the built artifact set against the names derived from this list for exact set equality (no globbing).

os.description: Operating system family. Naming segment <os> uses this value verbatim.

osVersionRange.description: Supported OS version range for this target. windows: Windows build range (>=10.0.17763 = Windows 10 1809, WebView2-capable floor; calibrated in P5-03). macos: macOS version range (>=13.5 per D5). linux: the oldest supported baseline of the D2 set (>=22.04, i.e. Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35 floor); artifacts are distro-independent, the value only pins the build/verify baseline.

arch.description: Machine architecture. windows/macos use Node-style names (x64, arm64); linux uses triple-style names (x86_64, aarch64) - narrowed per os by the conditional rules below. 32-bit values (ia32, x86, armv7l) are deliberately absent (D1).

variant.description: bootstrap: runtime prerequisites come from the system (Windows WebView2 Evergreen with an in-archive bootstrapper sidecar for repair; Linux system WebKitGTK). offline: prerequisites carried in the package (Windows bundles the Fixed Version runtime as webview2-runtime/; Linux self-contained bundle).

targetTriple.description: Rust target triple of the Tauri shell build for this target.

webviewStrategy.description: WebView provisioning strategy; the os/variant-coherent value is enforced semantically by @xresconv/packaging. windows bootstrap: webview2-evergreen (system Evergreen runtime expected, shell preflights it and guides to the in-archive bootstrapper when missing). windows offline: webview2-fixed-runtime (Fixed Version runtime bundled in the archive as webview2-runtime/, shell points the loader at it via WEBVIEW2_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_FOLDER and applies the Win10 AppContainer ACL). macos: system-only (WKWebView ships with the OS, D5). linux bootstrap: webkitgtk-system (WebKitGTK 4.1 from the distro, preflight.sh guides). linux offline: webkitgtk-bundled (WebKitGTK/GTK and transitive deps carried in the self-contained package).

minimumWebview.description: Minimum acceptable webview version gate. windows: WebView2 runtime floor 120.0.0 (frontend build target chrome120 in apps/desktop/vite.config.ts). macos: null (no separate webview version; the osVersionRange floor is the gate, D5). linux: WebKitGTK library floor 2.38 (API 4.1; feature gate calibrated on clean VMs in P5-05/P5-06).

nodeVersion.description: Bundled Node.js major line shipped inside every variant (repo engines: >=24.0.0). The exact version and its hash are pinned at build time into runtime-manifest.json (nodeVersion/nodeHash there).
